record.paper_title: Advances in periodic difference equations with open problems
record.original_question: Consider the periodically forced harvesting model x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n) − h_n, where {h_n} is a periodic sequence of harvesting quotas. If one is free to permute the order of the quotas while keeping the same multiset of values, which permutation is most favorable to the population, both in terms of enlarging the basin of attraction and in terms of maximizing the arithmetic average of the attractor?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7.2. Consider Eq. (7.1) with harvesting (i.e. −hn). Investigate the effect of ordering the elements of the sequence {hn} on the population. On other words, assume that we have a periodic sequence of harvesting quotas but we have the freedom to permute its elements. Which permutation of {hn} plays on the advantage of the population in terms of the basin of attraction and in terms of the arithmetic average of the attractor?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f:[0,∞)→(0,∞) be a continuous function such that the map x↦x f(x) models the per-capita reproduction of a population. Consider the periodically forced harvesting difference equation
    x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n) − h_n,  n = 0,1,2,…,
where {h_n} is a p-periodic sequence of nonnegative harvesting quotas (i.e., h_{n+p}=h_n for all n) taken from a fixed multiset H = {h^{(1)}, h^{(2)}, …, h^{(p)}} of p nonnegative real numbers. For each permutation σ of {1,…,p}, define the σ-ordered system by setting h_n = h^{(σ(n mod p)+1)}, which produces a p-periodic non-autonomous dynamical system whose composition map admits (under appropriate hypotheses) a globally attracting p-cycle A_σ ⊂ [0,∞) with basin of attraction B_σ ⊂ [0,∞).

Determine which permutation σ of the multiset H is most favorable to the population in the following two senses:
(a) σ maximizes (in the sense of set inclusion or of size) the basin of attraction B_σ of the attracting p-cycle of the harvested system;
(b) σ maximizes the arithmetic mean (1/p)·Σ_{x ∈ A_σ} x of the points of the attracting p-cycle.

Characterize the optimal permutation(s) for each of the two criteria, and compare them.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open in general. Related research has studied permutation effects on attractors of periodic Beverton–Holt-type models (e.g., grouping permutations into dihedral equivalence classes that yield identical geometric-mean populations), but no general characterization of optimal permutations of harvesting quotas with respect to both basin of attraction and arithmetic mean of the attractor has been established.

status_evidence.title: The effect of maps permutation on the global attractor of a periodic Beverton–Holt model
status_evidence.snippet: Studies how permuting maps in a periodic Beverton–Holt model affects the global attractor; permutations partition into dihedral equivalence classes producing the same geometric mean.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on related permutation questions for periodic harvesting/Beverton–Holt models exists, but the original problem about optimal ordering of harvesting quotas for both basin and arithmetic mean is not fully resolved.
